profile.headline: Engineering @ Confluent | Prev @ Dropbox, VMware
profile.summary: Experienced Software Engineer with a demonstrated history of working in the computer software industry. Skilled in Distributed Systems, Cloud Native Systems, Kubernetes, Docker, Storage, Ultra Low Latency and Databases. Strong engineering professional with a Master of Science (M.S.) focused in Computer Science from Stony Brook University.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Building sharing products to allow Dropbox users to collaborate and share content across users and teams, focusing on receiving experience of content sharing paradigm
- Building Dropbox's cloud documents platform powering integrations like Microsoft Office 365, Google Docs, Sheets, Slides and Dropbox Paper

positions.title: Member of Technical Staff 3
positions.description: Building VMware vSphere incumbent service to support persistent volume provisioning and monitoring exclusively for cloud native orchestrators like Kubernetes and DockerSwarm

positions.title: Member Of Technical Staff 2
positions.description:
•	Contributed towards Kubernetes - VMware Cloud Provider to leverage VMware storage offering
•	Worked on developing Docker volume plugin to enable persistent volume storage on VMware vSAN and VMFS
•	Prototyped an application agnostic Backup and Cloning solution for cloud native application with persistent storage requirements exclusive deployed on VMware infrastructure

Open source contributions on behalf of VMware - https://github.com/pshahzeb

positions.title: Intern - Member of Technical Staff
positions.description: Core Storage Team under Storage and Availability Business Unit

positions.title: Software Developer Analyst 2
positions.description:
Worked closely with Global Market Access team which involved delivering a C++ based market access application. Following are significant deliveries:

• Developed a cross-middleware messaging tool that would allow message exchanges across different middlewares like Tibco EMS, Informatica UME, TCP, MC.
• Developed a feature to enhance data persistence and replicate data across network. Made use of SCTP protocol to leverage stream based data transfer across multiple nodes in a distributed persistence system.
• Responsible for developing and maintenance of components like Work Queue Manager, Data Persistence, Event Dispatcher, Messaging, Resource Managers which formed the backbone of Market Access applications.
• Did an exhaustive case study of MongDB, Redis, Cassandra and GemFire for data management and persistence.

positions.title: Software Developer Analyst 1
positions.description:
After my undergraduation, I joined Citi in the Core Technology Team within Global Market Access Team.

• Developed a Parser and Code Generator using C++ Boost Libraries for automatic code generation based on grammar files. This was instrumental in providing data serialization and deserialization feature in market access applications.
• Developed asynchronous variants of event dispatchers, work queue managers and messaging handlers. 
• Engineered a Continuous Integration Framework that encompassed various tools to perform static code analysis, dynamic code analysis and code coverage.
• Did an evaluation of Tibco FTL as a messaging middleware solution. Also integrated it along with other middlewares like Tibco EMS, Informatica UME into market access applications. 
• Involved in unit, integration and performance testing of code. Also simulated a distributed environment across multiple nodes to perform stress testing and finding out round trip latency of order data sent and received.
• Made use of best possible design patters, assembly level optimization and heuristics based optimization in applications to improve latency and do operations in nanoseconds.

projects.title: Distributed Policy Evaluation of History based Access Control Policies
projects.description:
•	Implemented a distributed algorithm to evaluate access controls where decision depends on past history/updates. Algorithm is scalable as described in http://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=2818008
•	Improved the approach by using multiversion concurrency control and timestamp ordering to achieve 20% performance improvement

projects.title: Optimal Network Bandwidth allocation to virtual machines based on predictive analysis
projects.description:
•	Designed a smart strategy based on the network bandwidth consumed by each virtual machine to extrapolate the future requirement
•	Developed a python tool to control ingress and outgress bandwidth cap of network bandwidth for a virtual machine dynamically based on the calculations to make efficient usage of available network bandwidth on a physical node
•	Successfully implemented the solution on KVM Hypervisor and results proved 30% reduction in bottlenecks

publications.title: OBM - An Optimal Bandwidth Management Strategy to Virtual Machines in Cloud Environment Using Predictive Analytics
publications.publisher: IEEE International Cloud Computing Conference for Emerging Markets · Oct 18, 2013
